```{r MULTI FS RF FUNCTION PROTOTYPE}
rf_control_function = function(df,
                               target,
                               k1,
                               k2,
                               num_repeats,
                               threshold,
                               n_top_features = c()
){
  cl = makeCluster(6)
  registerDoParallel(cl)
    
  external_perf_df = NULL
  global_perf_df = NULL
  
  external_conf_table_list = list()
  global_conf_table_list = list()
  
  external_coef_df = NULL
  global_coef_df = NULL
  
  
  threshold_df = df %>% filter(Conc. > threshold) %>% 
    select(-c(Conc., Replicates))
  
  num_feature_array = c(1, n_top_features)
  
  for (rep in 1:num_repeats){
    global_kfold = createFolds(threshold_df[[target]], k = k1)
    
    for (global_fold in 1:k1) {
      global_train = threshold_df[-global_kfold[[global_fold]], ]
      global_test = threshold_df[global_kfold[[global_fold]], ]
      
      external_resample = rf_resampling_function(
        target = target,
        dataset = global_train,
        n_folds = k2,
        perf_df = external_perf_df,
        coef_df = external_coef_df,
        conf_table_list = external_conf_table_list,
        transformation = c("scale", "center")
        )
      external_perf_df = external_resample$perf_df
      external_coef_df = external_resample$coef_df
      external_conf_table_list = external_resample$conf_table_list
    }
    # Next I need to average the importance and identify the top n pairs
    # SORTING COEFS AND DOWNSELECTING GLOBAL DF BASED ON EXTERNAL RESAMPLING
  #   Easier just to call this regardless since it's really fast   
      avg_coefs = data.frame("avg_importance" = colMeans(external_coef_df))
      avg_coefs = avg_coefs %>% arrange(desc(avg_importance))
      avg_coefs$Pairs = row.names(avg_coefs)
      
      max_features = length(avg_coefs$avg_importance)
      num_feature_array[1] = max_features
      num_feature_array = num_feature_array[which(num_feature_array <= max_features)]
      print(num_feature_array)
      global_resample = multi_feature_global_rf_resampling(
        target = target,
        train = global_train,
        test = global_test,
        sorted_coefs = avg_coefs,
        num_feature_list = num_feature_array,
        perf_df = global_perf_df,
        coef_df = global_coef_df,
        conf_table_list = global_conf_table_list,
        transformation = c("scale", "center")
      )
      global_conf_table_list = global_resample$conf_table_list
      global_coef_df = global_resample$coef_df
      global_perf_df = global_resample$perf_df
  }
  
  return(list("external_conf_tables" = external_conf_table_list,
              "external_coef_df" = external_coef_df,
              "external_performance" = external_perf_df,
              "global_conf_tables" = global_conf_table_list,
              "global_coef_df" = global_coef_df,
              "global_performance" = global_perf_df,
              "global_coef_plot" = global_coef_plot
              ))
}
```

```{r}
multi_fs_parser_rf = function(mixed_performance_df, dab){
  
  std.err = function(x, na.rm = T) sd(x, na.rm)/sqrt(length(x))
  
  fs_data = mixed_performance_df %>% filter(!global_iterations %in% c("Average","Stdev"))
  
  fs_data_avg = fs_data %>%
    select(accuracy, kappa, Average_f1, num_features) %>% 
    group_by(num_features) %>%
    summarise(across(everything(), .f = list(mean = mean, se = std.err), na.rm = T))
  
  colnames(fs_data_avg) = c(
    "num_features",
    "Mean Accuracy",
    "accuracy_se",
    "Mean Kappa",
    "kappa_se",
    "Mean Average F1",
    "Average_f1_se"
  )
  # Braindead way of doing this becuase gathers been deprecated for forever,
  # pivot_longer would be better but I can't be bothered right now
  fs_avg_long = fs_data_avg %>%
    gather(mean_type, mean_val, "Mean Accuracy", "Mean Kappa", "Mean Average F1") %>%
    gather(se_type, se_val, accuracy_se, kappa_se, Average_f1_se) %>% 
    distinct(mean_val, .keep_all = T)
  

  viz = ggplot(fs_avg_long, aes(num_features, y = mean_val, colour=mean_type)) + 
    geom_line() + 
    geom_point() + 
    geom_errorbar(aes(ymin=mean_val-se_val, ymax=mean_val+se_val), width = 0.2)+
    scale_x_reverse(breaks = seq(max(fs_data$num_features), min(fs_data$num_features),  by = -1))+
    ylim(0.2, 1.0) +
    labs(title = paste('Average Performance by number of pairs used in the model - ', dab),
         x = "Number of antibody pairs in model",
         y = "Mean performance metric value",
         color = "Performance Metric") +
    theme_classic()+
    scale_color_brewer(palette = 'Dark2')
  
  return(list("avg_df" = fs_avg_long,
              "plot" = viz))
}
```

#shit ass rf_train function of yore for reference
```{r, ranger_cv_function}
# Outer cross-validation loop is the training data (recombinant) and testing data is 
# the clinical data

# The secondary cross-validation loop k-fold cross-validation of the recombinant data. This 
# includes validation of the model trained in the tertiary loop, and subsequent feature
# selection

# The tertiary cross-validation loop is k-fold CV via caret or glmnet

recombinant_cv = function(clinical_df, recombinant_df, target, class_dist = F,
                          model_type, tune_grid, train_control){
  # I can pretty easily modify this function to be a generalized method by adding
  # a tune grid and a model method argument.
  # Class distance indicates whether the training and testing sets should be 
  # modified to include the Mahalanobis class distances as additional predictors
  confusion_list = list()
  model_list = list()
  mod_index = 1
  
  best_tunes = NULL
  internal_pred_df = NULL
  
  if (class_dist == T){
    class_distances = getCentroids(recombinant_df, clinical_df, target)
    clinical_df = cbind(clinical_df, class_distances$test_distances)
    recombinant_df = cbind(recombinant_df, class_distances$train_distances)
  }
  
  x_clinical_test = clinical_df %>% dplyr::select(-target)
  y_clinical_test = clinical_df$Variant
  
  global_train_folds = createFolds(recombinant_df[[target]], k=5)
  
  for (fold in 1:length(global_train_folds)){
    global_train = recombinant_df[-global_train_folds[[fold]],]
    global_test = recombinant_df[global_train_folds[[fold]],]
    
    x_global_train = global_train %>% dplyr::select(-target)
    y_global_train = global_train[[target]]
    
    x_global_test = global_test %>% dplyr::select(-target)
    y_global_test = global_test[[target]]
    
    internal_mod = train(x = x_global_train,
                         y = y_global_train,
                         # preProc = c("center", "scale"),
                         method = model_type,
                         trControl = train_control,
                         metric = 'Kappa',
                         tuneGrid = tune_grid)
    
    # Using the final model obtained in the cross validation, predict on the left out data
    internal_preds = predict(internal_mod$finalModel, x_global_test, 
                             type = 'response')
    
    accuracy = sum(ifelse(internal_preds$predictions == y_global_test,
                          1, 0))/
      length(y_global_test)
    
    tune_acc = cbind(internal_mod$bestTune, accuracy)
    
    # Adds best tuning parameters onto the tuning parameters dataframe
    if (is.null(best_tunes)){
      best_tunes = tune_acc
    }
    else {
      best_tunes = rbind(best_tunes, tune_acc)
    }
    
    confusionTable = confusionMatrix(data = internal_preds$prediction, 
                                     reference = y_global_test)
    model_list[[mod_index]] = c(model_list, internal_mod)
    confusion_list[[mod_index]] = c(confusion_list, confusionTable)
    mod_index = mod_index + 1
  }
  
  x_recombinant_full = recombinant_df %>% dplyr::select(-target)
  y_recombinant_full = recombinant_df[[target]]
  
  clinical_model = train(x = x_recombinant_full,
                         y = y_recombinant_full,
                         trControl = train_control,
                         method = model_type,
                         metric = 'Kappa',
                         tuneGrid = tune_grid)
  
  clinical_preds = predict(clinical_model$finalModel, x_clinical_test,
                           type = 'response')
  
  clinical_confusion = confusionMatrix(data = clinical_preds$predictions,
                                       reference = y_clinical_test)
  
  return(list("model_list" = model_list,
              "tuner" = best_tunes,
              "confusionMats" = confusion_list,
              "final_model" = c(clinical_model),
              "testConfusionMat" = clinical_confusion))
}
```

rf_resampling_function = function(target,
                                  dataset,
                                  n_folds,
                                  perf_df,
                                  coef_df,
                                  conf_table_list,
                                  transformation){
  # Function is almost identical to the lasso resample function, with the 
  # exception that instead of a model list we pass a data frame of coefficients.
  # The model list in the lasso resampling function is essentially only used to
  # generate coefficients, so this cuts out the middle man
  model_formula = paste(target, "~", ".") %>% as.formula()
  
  folds = createFolds(dataset[[target]], k = n_folds)
  
  train_contrl = trainControl(method = "repeatedcv",
                          number = 5,
                          repeats = 3)
  
  for (fold in 1:n_folds){
    train = dataset[-folds[[fold]], ]
    test = dataset[folds[[fold]], ]
    
    preprocess = preProcess(train, method = transformation)
    train = predict(preprocess, train)
    test = predict(preprocess, test)
    
    x_train = train %>% select(-target)
    y_train = train[[target]]
    
    x_test = test %>% select(-target)
    y_test = test[[target]]
    
    rf_train = train(model_formula,
                     data = x_train,
                     method = "ranger",
                     importance = "impurity",
                     trControl = train_contrl,
                     verbose = T)
    
    opt_predict = predict(rf_train$finalModel, x_test,
                          type = 'response')
    opt_predict = opt_predict$predictions %>% as.factor()
    
    perf_call = get_rf_performance(opt_predict, y_test)
    
    coef_imp = varImp(rf_train)
    # Transposing the matrix is perfect, since it makes the row names the colnames
    # which can then be passed to bind_rows. Bind_rows is ideal because it matches
    # by column name.
    coef_imp = as.data.frame(t(coef_imp$importance))
    
    if (is.null(perf_df)){
      perf_df = perf_call$perf_metrics
    }
    else{
      perf_df = bind_rows(perf_df, perf_call$perf_metrics)
    }
    
    if (is.null(coef_df)){
      coef_df = coef_imp
    }
    else{
      coef_df = coef_df %>% bind_rows(coef_imp)
    }
    conf_table_list[[length(conf_table_list)+1]] = perf_call$conf_matrix
    
  }
  return(list("perf_df" = perf_df,
              "coef_df" = coef_df,
              "conf_table" = conf_table_list))
}
